subject: Request: temporary burst & overage credit for launch spike
messages:
From: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@brightlinehealth.com>
To: alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: peter.morales@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst & overage credit for launch spike

Alex —

Quick heads up: we saw a surge this morning when our new onboarding flow went live. Usage hit ~7x our forecast during a 3-hour window and we started getting 429s. We temporarily throttled client-side retry logic to avoid more errors, but the spike did cause a meaningful overrun of our monthly quota.

Can Redwood enable a one-week burst capacity and confirm how overage will be billed? We’re launching a pilot with 25k users this week; predictable behavior is critical. Ideally we’d convert the burst into a short-term upgrade and roll the overage into our next invoice (or apply a one-time credit).

I’ve attached a short CSV with per-minute token usage for the 22nd. Please advise on options and any contract steps needed.

Amanda Chen
Head of Product, Brightline Health
amanda.chen@brightlinehealth.com
[attachment: usage_report_may2026.csv (csv)]

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Amanda Chen <amanda.chen@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 14:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst & overage credit for launch spike

Amanda — thanks for the quick report and the CSV. Sorry you ran into 429s on launch day. We can absolutely help; proposed next steps below so we can move fast: 

1) Immediate: enable a temporary burst policy for Brightline that raises your per-route rate limits and token quota for 7 days to cover the pilot window (no infra changes on your side).

2) Billing: we can either (A) bill overage at standard overrun rates and then apply a one-time credit, or (B) treat the burst as an interim \"upgrade\" for the week at a pre-agreed capped price and then true-up on the next invoice. I recommend option B for predictability during the launch.

3) Credit: I’ll propose a one-time credit equal to 30% of the calculated overage if you choose option B and sign the short MSA amendment for temporary capacity (DocuSign link to follow).

Connor — can you confirm the exact limit increases and the activation ETA? Vivek/Laura — can you review the pricing approach; I flagged this under DL-8472.

Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Office: +1 415-555-0191

Subject: Re: Request: temporary burst & overage credit for launch spike

Thanks Alex / Amanda — I dug into the CSV. Short technical summary: the surge is bursty (sharp 3-hour peak) with high short-lived concurrency on the primary /generate route. We can: 

- Raise the per-route concurrency cap from 50 -> 250 and the token soft-quota from 10M/day -> 60M/day for 7 days. That will remove the 429s and maintain low latency.
- Enable temporary prefix caching for common prompts to shave repeat token cost during the peak.

Activation ETA: we can flip the policy in our control plane within ~30 minutes once legal approves the amendment. I attached an excerpted usage CSV in case you want a quick visualization.

[attachment: usage_report_may2026.csv (csv)]

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alex / Laura — I reviewed the numbers and the DL-8472 commercial terms. Proposal for internal approval and to present to Brightline: 

- One-week burst increase as described by Connor.
- Billing model: temporary upgrade (flat weekly fee) at $2,400 for the burst week, instead of ad-hoc per-token overage billing. This is a capped charge.
- One-time customer credit: 30% credit applied to the burst-week fee (net $1,680) if Brightline signs the MSA amendment within 72 hours.
- True-up: any additional sustained increase beyond 7 days rolls into the next monthly tier discussion and is subject to normal tier pricing.

I’ve attached the short MSA amendment PDF (legal-approved language) and a link to the DocuSign envelope. If Laura approves I’ll send the DocuSign and coordinate billing.

Vivek Kulkarni
